title: How to exercise safely in hot weather
facts: Players at the 2026 World Cup in the US, Canada, and Mexico received hydration breaks 22 minutes into each half.
Christian García-Witulski is an environmental lifestyle epidemiologist at the Pontifical Catholic University of Argentina.
Research by Christian García-Witulski estimates reduced physical activity from rising heat could cause 470,000 to 700,000 premature deaths annually by 2050.
Ollie Jay serves as the director of the Heat and Health Research Centre at the University of Sydney.
Ollie Jay stated that during exercise in heat, blood diverted to the skin reduces oxygen delivery to muscles.
Direct sunlight can increase experienced temperatures by 12 to 15 degrees Celsius compared to shaded areas.
High humidity impairs the body's cooling mechanism by reducing the evaporation rate of sweat from skin.
Rebecca Stearns is a kinesiologist at the Korey Stringer Institute at the University of Connecticut.
Rebecca Stearns stated that ice packs have a low cooling rate because they cover only small areas of skin.
Researchers developed a free digital heat risk assessment tool covering more than 40 different sports.
Immersion cooling involves submerging body parts such as hands and forearms into cold water.
Consuming ice slurry before physical exertion lowers baseline body temperature and improves exercise performance in heat.
Heat acclimatization adaptations typically develop after seven to 14 days of consistent exercise in high temperatures.
Regular heat acclimatization leads to a lower resting core body temperature, increased sweat rate, and expanded blood plasma volume.
Elite athletes face high heatstroke risks because of their propensity to exert effort beyond normal biological limits.
